family.description: This domain is often found in association with the kinase domains [pfam:PF00069] or [pfam:PF07714]. In many proteins it is duplicated. It contains six conserved cysteines which are involved in disulphide bridges [[cite:PUB00052808]]. It has a role in salt stress response [[cite:PUB00109166]] and has antifungal activity [[cite:PUB00109167]].

causal_graphs.context: Mature Ala1-Phe108 plus an extra N-terminal Met, expressed periplasmically in E. coli BL21(DE3) using pET26b and pDsbABCD1. Untagged protein purified by SP Sepharose, Mono S and Superdex 75. Immobilize from 50 ug/ml acetate pH6 onto a noncarbohydrate GLH chip at approximately 10000 RU; ProteOn XPR36 running buffer is 10 mM HEPES pH7 and 150 mM NaCl. Methods give analyte 1.25-20 mM, whereas Figure 5 labels 0.625-10 mM; the twofold discrepancy remains unresolved. Assays described as triplicate.

evidence.explanation: Figure 5 WT dose series was visually inspected with SPR Results and Methods. The figure and Methods concentration ranges disagree by twofold.
Current domain coordinates and exact UniProt/InterPro/4XRE sequence comparisons verify mature-protein scope and the three residue offsets.

edges.mechanism: Higher labeled mannobiose doses yield larger WT sensor responses. This directly supports a concentration-dependent biochemical interaction, with no precise affinity recalculation or claim that monosaccharide mannose was measured by SPR.
edges.subject: wt-mannobiose-dose

evidence.explanation: Figure 5 N11A and WT sensorgrams visually support reduced responses with residual binding; Results reports CD controls whose supplementary figure was not visually inspected.
evidence.snippet: markedly decreased compared with the wild-type protein

edges.mechanism: N11A gives smaller mannobiose sensor responses than WT over the displayed matched dose series, but retains nonzero responses. This is the net substitution effect, not proof that only one hydrogen bond or the isolated Pfam domain changed.
edges.subject: n11a

evidence.explanation: Figure 5 R93A versus WT, SPR Methods and Results; the separate yeast/Fusarium assays are not a continuous molecular trajectory.
evidence.snippet: markedly decreased compared with the wild-type protein

edges.mechanism: R93A strongly reduces the mannobiose sensor response relative to WT. Low signals prevent a fitted mutant affinity, rather than establishing mathematically zero binding or direct fungal lethality.
edges.subject: r93a

evidence.explanation: Figure 5 E104A/WT comparison was visually inspected; no N11A/E104A growth curves are supplied by this study.
evidence.snippet: markedly decreased compared with the wild-type protein

edges.mechanism: E104A produces smaller mannobiose sensor responses than WT. The assay supports the substitution's biochemical effect but not a measured E104A antifungal phenotype or a unique atomic explanation.
edges.subject: e104a

causal_graphs.family_mapping: A4ZDL6 sequence version 1 is 134 aa; mature 1-108 corresponds to precursor 27-134. UniProt/InterPro sequences match, with current PF01657 36-131, or mature 10-105. N11/R93/E104 correspond to precursor N37/R119/E130, all within that interval. PDB 4XRE entity 1 exactly matches Met plus the mature reference. This is a domain-bearing mature protein, not an isolated Pfam-interval construct.
causal_graphs.limitations: Responses are directly observed binding-assay effects, not activation of another protein or fungal killing. N11A retains visible response; low mutant signals do not establish zero affinity. The reported WT KD of 5.9 +/- 0.2 mM is not independently verified, especially given the dose discrepancy. The authors report similar mutant CD spectra, but supplementary S5 was not visually accessible here; immobilized active fractions and local folding are not independently established. Static mannose contacts do not directly observe the mannobiose binding trajectory.

causal_graphs.context: BY4741 MATa his3delta1 leu2delta0 met15delta0 ura3delta0, potato dextrose broth at 25 C. Transfer pre-culture at OD600 1 into fresh medium at OD600 0.01 with 2 uM WT/R93A or no protein. Monitor OD600 until 2.55. The WT-plus-saccharide arms contain 0.5% w/v yeast mannan or 50 mM D-mannose. Methods state two repetitions; Figure 7 shows growth curves without statistical confidence intervals.

evidence.explanation: Figure 7A curves visually inspected with yeast Methods and Discussion; baseline, dose, medium and timing are explicit.
evidence.snippet: Gnk2 prolonged the lag phase of yeast growth

edges.mechanism: WT-treated cultures enter their OD600 rise much later than the no-protein control. The measured effect is lag extension, not an inferred molecular lesion or a permanently lower exponential growth rate.
edges.subject: wt-treatment

evidence.explanation: Figure 7A WT/R93A/no-protein comparisons and Results; the residual delay remains visible rather than being labeled complete inactivity.
evidence.snippet: Gnk2 prolonged the lag phase of yeast growth

edges.mechanism: R93A-treated cultures have much less delay than WT-treated cultures, with a small residual delay relative to the untreated control. Loss of all activity or equal binding-site-specific effects on every other protein property are not asserted.
edges.subject: r93a-treatment

evidence.explanation: Figure 7A WT-plus-mannan versus WT-alone curves and 0.5% Methods condition; the 50 mM mannose arm has little attenuation and is retained as a condition-specific negative.
evidence.snippet: Gnk2 prolonged the lag phase of yeast growth

edges.mechanism: Soluble yeast mannan strongly attenuates the growth delay seen with WT Gnk2 alone. The result is consistent with ligand competition, but the cellular assay does not uniquely distinguish it from other effects of added mannan.
edges.subject: soluble-mannan

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Purified mature A4ZDL6 residues 27-134 plus extra N-terminal Met; current PF01657 36-131 corresponds to mature 10-105. Mature R93 maps to precursor R119 inside the domain. The yeast is the assay organism, not the source of this Ginkgo protein.
causal_graphs.limitations: Turbidity delay is indirect physiology, not direct cell-wall damage, killing or measured spore germination. The Discussion specifies longer lag rather than reduced log-phase growth rate. R93A and mannan attenuation are not complete null effects. Saccharide-only controls are not displayed, so competitive sequestration is an interpretation, not a uniquely established causal step. Similar R93A thermal stability and mannan NMR results are author-reported supplementary controls, not visually inspected here.

causal_graphs.scope: S. cerevisiae BY4741 exposed to purified mature Ginkgo Gnk2; Miyakawa 2014 Figure 7A, not the delta-mnn2 culture or an in-plant infection test.
causal_graphs.title: WT Gnk2 delays BY4741 growth, with attenuation by R93A or soluble mannan

causal_graphs.context: Potato dextrose broth, 25 C, initial OD600 0.01, 2 uM WT Gnk2, OD600 followed to 2.55. MNN2 encodes an N-linked-glycan alpha1,2-mannosyltransferase; deletion alters those mannosylated branches, not all cell-wall mannan. No MNN2 complementation is shown.

evidence.explanation: Figure 7A/B were visually compared with yeast Methods and Results; the small residual delta-mnn2 delay qualifies the text's no-effect statement.
evidence.snippet: Gnk2 prolonged the lag phase of yeast growth

edges.mechanism: The additional growth delay caused by WT Gnk2 is markedly smaller in delta-mnn2 than in the parental strain. This supports a glycosylation-background-dependent phenotype, not total mannan absence or a directly observed binding-to-wall-damage chain.
edges.subject: mnn2-deletion-background

causal_graphs.family_mapping: The applied protein is mature Ginkgo A4ZDL6 plus extra Met, with PF01657 at precursor 36-131. The genetic perturbation is in the target yeast, not in Gnk2 or its Pfam domain.
causal_graphs.limitations: The edge compares treatment responses against each strain's own baseline, not simply absolute treated-culture growth. Figure 7B has a small residual delay, so the Results' no-influence wording is not adopted literally. No rescue or direct glycan occupancy measurement isolates the deleted gene's immediate molecular effect. Delta-och1 was too growth impaired to assay and is not evidence of Gnk2 resistance.

causal_graphs.title: The delta-mnn2 yeast background strongly attenuates the Gnk2 growth delay

causal_graphs.context: Potato dextrose broth at 25 C, initial OD600 0.005; 2 or 10 uM WT/R93A; measure OD600 after 36 h. Inhibition is relative to the no-protein endpoint. Figure 8C gives means and SD with n=3; no new statistical analysis is performed.

evidence.explanation: Figure 8C bars were visually inspected with fungal Methods and the numerical Results; the assay is a 36-h endpoint despite the Methods' growth-rate terminology.

edges.mechanism: WT Gnk2 lowers the 36-h OD600 endpoint relative to the no-protein control, corresponding to 68.2% inhibition at 10 uM. The lower 2-uM dose shows a smaller effect; neither measurement identifies a unique downstream molecular mechanism.
edges.subject: wt-liquid-treatment

evidence.explanation: Figure 8C WT/R93A bars at matched 10-uM dose and the explicit Results values support attenuated, not abolished, inhibition.

edges.mechanism: At 10 uM, R93A produces much less endpoint inhibition than WT, 7.6% versus 68.2%. Residual activity prevents a complete-null claim, and this net protein-substitution effect is not a direct observation of cell-wall disruption.
edges.subject: r93a-liquid-treatment

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Ginkgo A4ZDL6 mature 1-108 corresponds to precursor 27-134, plus expression-derived Met. PF01657 36-131 contains R119, the precursor coordinate of mature R93. Whole mature protein is tested against F. culmorum, not an isolated domain or a fungal homolog.
causal_graphs.limitations: A 36-h turbidity endpoint is not a measured instantaneous growth rate, viability count or fungicidal mechanism. WT inhibits by 22.1% at 2 uM and 68.2% at 10 uM; R93A retains 7.6% inhibition at 10 uM. The reported 2-10-uM IC50 bracket is not a fitted exact value. Similar R93A stability is author-reported; no unique cellular lesion is demonstrated.

causal_graphs.context: Incubate at 25 C. Place 6-mm discs 5 mm from a roughly 30-mm colony, adding 30 ul of 10 mg/ml WT/R93A Gnk2 (300 ug) or 10 mM Tris pH7 buffer. Methods score 3 days after disc placement, whereas the caption reports 8 days after seeding; these timing origins can differ and are not assumed contradictory.

evidence.explanation: Figure 8A supplies the visually inspected WT-versus-buffer disc phenotype; Results contrasts it with R93A. The caption and Methods identify the 300-ug dose, strain and buffer control.

edges.mechanism: The WT disc has a local crescent of reduced mycelial advance compared with the buffer disc on the same plate. This is a spatial growth phenotype, not a measured cell-wall degradation reaction.
edges.subject: wt-disc

evidence.explanation: Figure 8A WT/R93A/control discs were visually inspected with its Results and fungal Methods; no numerical zone value is inferred from the photograph.

edges.mechanism: The R93A disc lacks the prominent WT-associated growth-exclusion crescent at the matched nominal dose. This qualitative comparison does not prove identical diffusion or absolute absence of activity.
edges.subject: r93a-disc

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Mature Ginkgo A4ZDL6 27-134 plus extra Met; current PF01657 36-131, including mature R93 at precursor119. This is a protein-dose experiment on a named fungal strain, not a family-wide antifungal claim.
causal_graphs.limitations: Qualitative plate morphology, without a reported zone diameter or independent viability measurement. Diffusion, stability and effective local concentration are not isolated. Figure 8A does not establish killing, a precise potency or the immediate cellular mechanism.

evidence.explanation: Figure 8B WT-versus-buffer discs were visually inspected, with Results contrasting R93A and the caption and Methods assigning the strain and disc dose.

edges.mechanism: The WT disc is associated with a local growth-exclusion crescent relative to the buffer disc on the same plate. The intervention supports a local antifungal phenotype, not an observed chemical wall-cleavage step.

edges.mechanism: R93A produces much less local growth exclusion than WT at the same nominal 300-ug dose. No completely inactive allele, identical diffusion or mechanistic link to the liquid-culture endpoint is assumed.

record.description: This domain is often found in association with the kinase domains [pfam:PF00069] or [pfam:PF07714]. In many proteins it is duplicated. It contains six conserved cysteines which are involved in disulphide bridges [[cite:PUB00052808]]. It has a role in salt stress response [[cite:PUB00109166]] and has antifungal activity [[cite:PUB00109167]].

evidence.explanation: Preserve Methods 1.25-20 versus Figure 5 0.625-10 mM mannobiose, small delta-mnn2 and R93A residual delays, lack of displayed saccharide-only controls, and separate disc/36-h endpoints. Supplementary CD/DSF/NMR controls are author-reported, not independently visually inspected. Historical domain 56-108 differs from current mature PF01657 10-105; all three tested residues lie within the current interval.
Later actin-remodeling study is a follow-up lead, not reviewed evidence for an added actin or cell-death edge. Early purification and other CRK/PDLP contexts also remain incomplete.

discussions.notes: NMR text reports mannose, glucose and N-acetylglucosamine responses, not exclusive mannose recognition; mannobiose docking, spore germination, wall damage, biofilm prevention and plant protection are not directly measured here. PDB 4XRE matches the reference and publication, but formal supersession of paper accession 3W9Q was not verified. Partial scientific self-review; IN_PROGRESS.
discussions.prompt: Resolve the SPR dose discrepancy and supplement access, then assess later Gnk2 actin work and other DUF26 members without assuming a common mechanism.
discussions.rationale: Four direct binding-assay effects and ten indirect growth effects support a scoped Gnk2 example, not a complete binding-to-cell-death trajectory or universal function of PF01657.
